episode_row: watchdog SIGABRT killed the scheduler every ~30 min (NRestarts=21)

commits.subject: fix(scheduler): emit notify_watchdog pings during SLEEPING-state waits
commits.body:
Bug: Three time.sleep calls in SLEEPING-state contexts (main-loop between
checks, fallback deadline wait, pre-result-polling wait) had no
notify_watchdog() pings during the sleep. Systemd's WatchdogSec=1800 (30
min) fires SIGABRT, killing the daemon.

Observed live 2026-04-23 overnight: NRestarts=21 since deploy of c43869d
yesterday 16:30. Every ~30:30 min exactly (matching WatchdogSec), the
scheduler was killed while in idle_end_of_day sleep → next-wake sleep.

Can't reuse _poll_interval_sleep's heartbeat_watchdog pattern here because
SLEEPING-state waits pre-write heartbeat with state=SLEEPING,
sleeping_until=X — overwriting that mid-sleep with state=RUNNING would
clobber metadata check_heartbeat.py needs for the "sleeping-fresh-until-
wake" rule. New helper _watchdog_ping_sleep just emits notify_watchdog()
every 60s without touching the heartbeat file.

Three call sites updated: lines for main-loop sleep, fallback deadline,
and pre-polling wait.

2 tests in TestWatchdogPingSleep: heartbeat file untouched, sleep duration
respected. Full suite 563 passed (was 561).
